name: Credit Score Gauge
hook: A needle sweeping to 742 with the four factors that moved it.
objective: Explain a credit score: the 300 to 850 range, band placement, the weighted factors, and what improves the score over time.
scenes: Score Range
The full 300 to 850 arc draws with band labels.
Semicircular gauge, five bands (Poor to Exceptional), tick labels every 100 points.
The arc draws from left to right over 900ms; band labels fade in sequentially; the needle sits at 300.
Needle Sweeps
The needle climbs to 742 in the Good band.
Needle from 300 to 742, a live numeric readout, a glow trail behind the needle.
The needle follows a damped spring with visible deceleration; the readout counts in lockstep; the trail decays over 300ms.
Factor Weights
Four weighted factors explain the score.
Four horizontal bars with weights 35%, 30%, 15%, 10% plus a 10% mix row.
Bars grow left to right at 100ms intervals; the weights sum visibly to 100% in a footer line.
Improvement Plan
Two specific actions project a 24-point increase.
Action cards with an explicit point effect, a projected needle ghost at 766.
A ghost needle renders at 40% opacity; action cards slide in at 120ms intervals; both needles hold at the end.
vectors: Semicircle 400px wide with a 14px stroke and rounded caps
Five arc segments with rose, amber, yellow, emerald and deep emerald fills
Tapered polygon 120px long with a 10px circular hub
Four 300x10 rounded bars with labels and mono percentages
Ghost needle at 40% opacity with a dashed outline
physics: The needle angle must be a pure function of the score, mapped across the 300 to 850 domain.
Factor weights must sum to exactly 100% including the catch-all row.
The projected needle is visually subordinate to the live needle; 40% opacity and dashed.
Damped spring on the needle means roughly 3% overshoot, no more, or it reads as inaccurate instrumentation.
data: const CREDIT = { score: 742, range: [300, 850], band: 'Good', factors: [{ name: 'Payment history', weight: 0.35 }, { name: 'Utilization', weight: 0.30 }, { name: 'History length', weight: 0.15 }, { name: 'Mix', weight: 0.10 }, { name: 'New credit', weight: 0.10 }], projected: 766, actions: ['Pay down 12% utilization', 'Dispute one late mark'] };
notes: State the scoring model once, in mono, in a corner. Score models differ and unlabeled gauges invite arguments.

name: BNPL Installments
hook: One purchase split into four payments across six weeks, with zero interest.
objective: Explain buy-now-pay-later mechanics: point-of-sale split, installment schedule, merchant discount fee, and late-fee policy.
scenes: Checkout Split
A $240 cart offers four payments of $60 at checkout.
Checkout panel, payment options list, a highlighted 4-payment row.
The BNPL row highlights with a 1.03 scale and a 2px indigo outline; the schedule preview fades in beneath.
Installment Schedule
Four payment nodes land across a six-week timeline.
Horizontal timeline with 4 nodes at day 0, 14, 28, 42, each with amount $60.00.
Nodes pop in chronological order at 140ms; the connecting timeline draws ahead of each node at 90% of its travel.
Merchant Fee
The merchant pays a 4.9% discount fee and receives $228.24 today.
Two-row settlement: customer pays 4x60, merchant receives 228.24 now, fee chip 11.76.
The fee chip lifts out of the total with an 8px rise and a rose tint; the merchant net figure counts in last.
Repaid
Three payments clear and the fourth completes the schedule.
Three settled nodes, a final PAID state, zero-interest badge throughout.
Each node ticks to settled at 200ms intervals; the zero-interest badge stays constant to reinforce the claim.
vectors: Horizontal rail 640px wide with 4 nodes and day labels
36px circles with a mono amount beneath and a status ring
340x200 with line items and a total in mono 32px
Rose pill with a signed percentage and an absolute figure
Emerald outline pill with a 0% glyph
physics: The four payments must sum exactly to the purchase total.
Merchant net plus fee must equal the purchase total, in the same currency.
Nodes settle only in chronological order; jumping ahead breaks the repayment narrative.
The zero-interest badge never animates or flashes. It is a constant, and constancy reads as reliability.
data: const BNPL = { cart: 240.00, currency: 'USD', installments: 4, perPayment: 60.00, apr: 0, merchantFeePct: 0.049, merchantFee: 11.76, merchantNet: 228.24, scheduleDays: [0, 14, 28, 42], lateFee: 7.00 };
notes: Show the merchant fee. BNPL demos that hide the merchant discount look like consumer advertising rather than explanation.

name: Invoice Factoring
hook: A 90-day invoice converting into 85% working capital today.
objective: Explain factoring and invoice financing: receivables aging, advance rate, discount fee, and settlement when the customer pays.
scenes: Invoice Aging
A $120,000 invoice sits at net-90 with an aging bar in amber.
Invoice card with terms NET 90, an aging bar, a cash gap indicator.
The aging bar fills over 1.2s across the 90-day span; the cash gap indicator pulses amber twice.
Advance Rate
The funder advances 85% immediately and holds 15% in reserve.
Advance figure $102,000, reserve $18,000, a split bar with 85/15 segments.
The split bar divides at 85% with a 240ms spring; both figures count in parallel on the same progress value.
Discount Fee
A 2.5% fee is disclosed against the reserve.
Fee chip $3,000, effective annualized cost note, a net settlement preview.
The fee chip slides out of the reserve segment; the annualized note fades in with a smaller type step.
Settled on Day 90
The customer pays, the reserve releases and the books close.
Day-90 marker, reserve release arrow, net cash $117,000, a reconciled badge.
The day-90 marker travels the aging bar; the reserve arrow reverses the earlier path; reconciled badge lands last.
vectors: 360x180 with invoice number, customer, amount and terms
Horizontal bar with 30/60/90 ticks and an amber fill
Single bar with an 85/15 cut and a divider tick
Curved arrow from reserve to operating balance
Emerald badge with a check glyph and a settlement date
physics: Advance plus reserve must equal the invoice total exactly.
The fee is drawn from the reserve, not from the invoice, and the visual must show that path.
The annualized cost of 2.5% over 90 days is roughly 10% APR; show it so the comparison is honest.
The reserve release uses a mirrored path to the advance so the round trip is legible.
data: const FACTORING = { invoice: 120_000, customer: 'Meridian Retail', termsDays: 90, advanceRate: 0.85, advance: 102_000, reserve: 18_000, feePct: 0.025, fee: 3_000, netSettled: 117_000, effectiveApr: 0.101 };
notes: Annualize the fee on screen. A 2.5% fee over 90 days is roughly a 10% annual cost, and hiding that is the deceptive pattern.

name: Payroll Distribution
hook: One treasury branching to fifty employees in a single orchestrated wave.
objective: Show bulk payroll disbursement: funding, batch validation, parallel payouts, and per-employee reconciliation status.
scenes: Treasury Funds
The company treasury shows $284,600 ready for the August payroll run.
Treasury card, payroll run ID, a funding status badge, 50-employee count.
The funding badge flips from PENDING to FUNDED with a 200ms crossfade; the amount counts in.
Batch Validation
The batch passes three validation gates before sending.
Three gates: balance check, duplicate check, tax withholding check.
Gates light in sequence at 400ms intervals; each returns a green pass chip that stays visible.
Parallel Payout
Fifty payments fan out simultaneously across three rails.
Central treasury node, 50 satellite employee nodes in a radial fan, rail color coding.
Arcs draw in a radial sweep from top to bottom over 1.4s; satellites activate in 8ms waves rather than one by one.
Reconciled
49 succeed, 1 is pending bank verification, and the batch reconciles.
49 emerald nodes, 1 amber node, a reconciliation summary and a retry action.
The amber node pulses twice; the summary counts 49/50; the retry chip fades in and holds.
vectors: 96px rounded square with a building glyph and a mono balance below
50 circles radius 8 on two concentric rings at r=180 and r=260
50 curves from center to satellites in three rail hues
Three rounded rects with a check slot and a lock glyph
Card with three counters: paid, pending, failed
physics: Fifty simultaneous arc draws must be batched by angle band, roughly 8 arcs per 120ms, or the browser will drop frames.
Satellite activation uses an 8ms cascade, which reads as simultaneous without the cost of 50 independent transitions.
Never render 50 individual DOM nodes with separate SVG filters; use one group filter and per-node opacity.
The pending node must remain visible in the final frame; a perfect 50/50 result is less credible than 49/50.
data: const PAYROLL = { runId: 'PR-2026-08', employees: 50, gross: 284_600, rails: ['ACH', 'RTP', 'Local'], paid: 49, pending: 1, failed: 0, totalPaid: 278_420, retryEta: 'Next window 02:00' };
notes: Performance is the risk here. Cap animated elements near 80 and reuse a single path template rather than creating 50 unique curves.

name: Expense Receipt OCR
hook: A crumpled receipt turning into structured expense fields.
objective: Show receipt OCR for expenses: image capture, field detection, extraction into structured data, category prediction and policy check.
scenes: Capture
The camera frames a receipt and auto-crops with perspective correction.
Phone viewfinder, receipt at an angle, four crop handles snapping to corners.
The crop quad deforms from screen-aligned to perspective-correct over 700ms; a subtle grid overlay appears.
Field Detection
Bounding boxes appear over vendor, date, total and tax.
Four dashed boxes with label tags, scanning line sweeping vertically.
The scan line sweeps top to bottom twice; each box draws after the line passes it, with a 120ms delay.
Extraction
Text lifts from the receipt into structured form fields.
Extraction ghosts flying from box to field, four form rows populating in mono.
Ghosts travel along a slight arc over 400ms; fields populate sequentially with a caret blink; confidence chips appear at 92% and above.
Policy Check
The expense is categorized, policy-checked and submitted.
Category chip MEALS, policy status WITHIN LIMIT, submit confirmation with an amount match.
Category chip types in; the policy check flips to emerald; a final match line confirms the total equals the sum of line items.
vectors: Rounded rect with 4 corner brackets and a 20% dim mask outside
Quadrilateral with draggable corner handles and hairline guides
Dashed rounded rects with label tabs anchored top-left
2px horizontal line with a gradient glow, clipped to the receipt
Four rows with label, mono value and a confidence chip
physics: Detection boxes appear only after the scan line has passed them; simultaneous appearance implies magic.
Extracted values use a light typing effect at 30 characters per second, not a hard cut.
Confidence is shown per field, and values below 90% visually flag for review.
The final total must equal the sum of detected line items; recompute at load.
data: const OCR = { vendor: 'Harbor Provisions', date: '2026-08-14', total: 84.36, tax: 6.12, category: 'Meals', confidence: { vendor: 0.97, date: 0.94, total: 0.99, tax: 0.91 }, policy: 'within $100 limit', currency: 'USD' };
notes: Keep the receipt content clearly synthetic. A real-looking receipt photo with a real vendor name can create legal friction in a demo.

name: Revenue-Based Financing
hook: A repayment bar that breathes with revenue instead of marching on a calendar.
objective: Explain RBF: an upfront advance, a fixed repayment multiple, a percentage of monthly revenue, and the true cost of capital.
scenes: Capital Advance
A $500,000 advance lands with a repayment cap of $650,000.
Advance card, a repayment multiple of 1.3x, a cap amount, terms summary.
The advance amount counts in over 500ms; the 1.3x multiple chip scales in at 200ms and stays fixed.
Revenue Share
Each month remits 8% of revenue and the bar tracks proportionally.
Monthly revenue bars rising and falling, a remittance overlay on each bar, a cumulative repaid counter.
Bars animate month by month at 320ms each; the remittance overlay grows with a 100ms lag; the cumulative counter follows.
Slow Month
A weak month means a smaller payment and a longer tail.
A short revenue bar, a visibly small remittance, the projected payoff date moving later.
The projected date slides right with a 300ms ease; the short bar renders at 40% height with a muted tint.
Fully Repaid
The cap is reached and the obligation ends, with the effective APR shown.
Cap reached badge, effective annualized cost 18.4%, total months 26.
The cumulative counter lands exactly on the cap; the effective-APR figure fades in last; hold.
vectors: Width 28, height mapped to revenue, 4px gap, at 30% opacity base fill
Same-width bar segment drawn from the base at 80% opacity in indigo
Mono 36px with a progress bar beneath
Date chip that translates along a horizontal rule
Emerald badge with a check and a total figure
physics: Remittance is always exactly the stated percentage of the rendered revenue bar; recompute per frame.
The cumulative counter must stop exactly at the cap, never overshoot.
The payoff date only moves later, never earlier, when revenue dips.
Show effective annualized cost at the end; RBF is cheaper than equity only sometimes, and the number should speak.
data: const RBF = { advance: 500_000, multiple: 1.3, cap: 650_000, revenueSharePct: 0.08, months: 26, strongMonth: 210_000, weakMonth: 96_000, effectiveApr: 0.184 };
notes: The effective APR is the honest counterweight to the friendly 'we only take a share' framing. Keep it in the final frame, not buried.

name: Cap Table Dilution
hook: Founder equity shrinking while the pie grows faster than it shrinks.
objective: Show dilution mechanics across rounds: pre and post-money, option pool expansion, founder dilution, and the absolute value effect.
scenes: Founding Cap Table
Two founders hold 100% split 60/40.
Pie with two segments, founder labels, a note that the pie equals 100%.
The pie draws clockwise over 700ms; segment labels fade in as each closes.
Seed Round
A $2M seed at $8M pre-money mints new shares and dilutes founders.
Pie with a new investor slice at 20%, a pre/post money band, a dilution note of -12.0% and -8.0%.
The pie re-slices with a 900ms interpolation; founder labels update only after the slice settles.
Option Pool
A 10% option pool is carved from the founders, not the investor.
An ESOP slice appearing between founders, a pool source annotation.
The ESOP slice grows from the founders' arcs specifically; a dashed leader line points to the source.
Series A
A $6M Series A at $24M pre-money lands, and absolute value still rises.
Pie with four segments, an absolute value callout showing founder stake worth more despite lower ownership.
The pie re-slices again; the value callout counts from $4.8M to $10.1M; the caption contrasts percent versus dollars and holds.
vectors: Circle r=150 with segments separated by 2px white gaps
Arc with a distinct hue and a subtle outer ring on first appearance
Hatched fill at 20% opacity to differentiate from cash ownership
Signed percentage chips anchored at segment midpoints
Card with two rows: ownership percent and dollar value
physics: All segments must sum to 100.0% after every round; compute and assert at load, not just visually.
Only the founders' arcs shrink when the pool is created, never the investor's.
Labels fade in only after their arc stops moving, otherwise the text smears.
The final scene must present percent and dollars together; dilution without value context is misleading.
data: const CAP_TABLE = { rounds: [{ name: 'Founding', founders: [0.60, 0.40], investor: 0, esop: 0 }, { name: 'Seed', founders: [0.48, 0.32], investor: 0.20, esop: 0 }, { name: 'Seed + Pool', founders: [0.43, 0.27], investor: 0.20, esop: 0.10 }, { name: 'Series A', founders: [0.3225, 0.2025], investor: 0.275, esop: 0.20 }], founderValueStart: 4_800_000, founderValueEnd: 10_100_000 };
notes: Verify every round's segments sum to 100%. Cap table demos are checked by finance people with a calculator in hand.

name: SaaS MRR Waterfall
hook: New, expansion and churn stacking into one honest net ARR number.
objective: Explain MRR movement: new business, expansion, contraction, churn, and net new MRR building to ending ARR.
scenes: Starting MRR
The opening balance of $412,000 stands as a solid column.
Single bar with a mono label and a baseline grid.
The bar grows from zero in 500ms; the label counts in with tabular-nums and locks.
Additions
New business and expansion stack upward in green.
Two stacked positive segments with labels NEW and EXPANSION, floating connector rules.
Each segment grows 0 -> full over 400ms at 200ms offsets; connector rules draw horizontally after each settles.
Subtractions
Contraction and churn pull down in rose.
Two negative segments with labels CONTRACTION and CHURN, descending connectors.
Segments drop on a 320ms ease-in; a 1px baseline marker indicates where the bar started so the net is readable.
Net ARR
The closing bar resolves to $446,800 with net new of $34,800.
Final bar, net new label, a growth rate of 8.4% MoM, an ARR annualization note.
The closing bar eases to its final height over 500ms; the net label fades in centered on the delta; hold.
vectors: Vertical bars 56px wide with 3px gaps and rounded 2px caps
Horizontal 1px dashed lines linking bar tops
1px line across the chart at 20% opacity
Vertical brace spanning the net change with a mono label
physics: Waterfall column heights must reconcile exactly: opening plus additions minus subtractions equals closing.
Negative segments start from the previous cumulative top, not from the baseline.
Connector rules draw only after the adjacent columns finish, so the eye follows the arithmetic.
Churn is never hidden in a net number; it gets its own visible segment.
data: const WATERFALL = { startMrr: 412_000, new: 38_400, expansion: 21_600, contraction: 9_200, churn: 16_000, netNew: 34_800, endMrr: 446_800, growthMoM: 0.084, endArr: 5_361_600 };
notes: The reconciliation is the entire point. Compute closing from the components at load and render that, so the chart cannot lie.

name: Usage-Based Billing
hook: An API meter ticking up and sliding between pricing tiers in real time.
objective: Explain metered billing: usage counters, tiered pricing blocks, graduated rate application, and the projected invoice.
scenes: Usage Meter
The meter starts at 0 and ticks up as API calls arrive.
Circular usage meter, live call counter, a mono rate of calls per second.
The counter increments in bursts of 3 to 5 with a 60ms cadence; the meter arc fills proportionally.
Tier Ladder
The usage crosses 100k and enters the second pricing block.
Four tier bands with unit prices, a marker crossing tier boundaries.
The marker slides along the ladder; on each boundary crossing the band under it brightens for 200ms and the effective rate updates.
Graduated Pricing
The invoice breaks into per-tier line items rather than one blended rate.
Four line items with usage per tier, unit price and subtotal, a blended effective rate.
Each line item grows in as its threshold is passed; the blended rate recomputes and re-renders each frame.
Projected Invoice
The month projects to $2,650.00 with the overage clearly separated.
Invoice summary, base commit $2,000, overage $650, projected total, a note on volume discount eligibility.
The summary sheet slides up 24px on a spring; totals count in; the discount hint fades in last.
vectors: Circle r=110 with a 10px stroke, dasharray mapped to the tier cap
Four horizontal bands with boundary ticks and mono unit prices
Four rows with usage, unit price, and right-aligned subtotal
Card with a base commit row, overage row and total rule
Mono counter with a small sparkline of the last 60 samples
physics: Graduated pricing means each tier's rate applies only within that tier; never multiply total usage by the top rate.
The invoice total must equal the sum of rendered line items, computed not hard-coded.
Tier boundary crossers pulse once and settle; repeated flashing makes the ladder feel unstable.
Use 4-decimal unit prices to keep small tiers visually meaningful.
data: const USAGE = { calls: 1_200_000, tiers: [{ upTo: 100_000, rate: 0.005 }, { upTo: 500_000, rate: 0.003 }, { upTo: 1_000_000, rate: 0.0015 }, { upTo: null, rate: 0.001 }], baseCommit: 2_000, overage: 650, projected: 2_650, effectiveRate: 0.0022 };
notes: Graduated and volume pricing are different models. Label which one is being shown, or the invoice math will be challenged.

name: Customs and Trade Finance
hook: A cargo ship unlocking a letter of credit at each supply-chain checkpoint.
objective: Show trade finance documentation: letter of credit issuance, checkpoint-based document release, and payment on bill of lading.
scenes: Letter of Credit
An importer's bank issues an LC for $480,000 to a supplier abroad.
LC document card with terms, issuing bank and beneficiary, a seal glyph.
The document slides in and the seal stamps with a 1.1 scale overshoot; the amount counts in.
Voyage
A ship travels a route across four checkpoints.
Route polyline across a simplified map, ship vector, four checkpoint nodes with labels.
The ship moves along the path via getPointAtLength; the route draws ahead by 8% so it never looks like the ship is ahead of the path.
Document Release
Each checkpoint unlocks one required document.
Four document chips unlocking sequentially: invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin.
Each chip flips from locked to released with a 180ms crossfade; the lock glyph rotates open 90deg.
Payment Released
All documents verified means funds release to the supplier.
Full document set, verification badge, payment rail to the supplier, a final LC status CLOSED.
The verification badge draws; the payment rail travels the reverse of the voyage path; status flips to CLOSED and holds.
vectors: Simplified landmass paths at 12% fill with a dotted route overlay
Top-down vessel outline 44x20 with a wake path trailing behind
24px circles with a flag glyph and a mono stage label
120x40 cards with a lock glyph and a document-type label
Gradient path from the issuing bank to the supplier
physics: The ship leads the path draw by exactly 8%, which reads as motion along a route rather than a race.
Documents unlock only at their specific checkpoint; batching them together destroys the causal story.
The wake trails 60px behind the ship and fades over 500ms.
Payment travels the reverse route to close the loop geometrically.
data: const TRADE = { lcAmount: 480_000, currency: 'USD', importer: 'Northline Trading', supplier: 'Andes Components', checkpoints: ['Port of Loading', 'Transit', 'Customs', 'Destination Port'], documents: ['Commercial Invoice', 'Packing List', 'Bill of Lading', 'Certificate of Origin'], incoterm: 'CIF', voyageDays: 34 };

name: Debt Snowball vs Avalanche
hook: Two payoff strategies racing to zero with different curves and the same finish line.
objective: Compare debt snowball and avalanche: ordering by balance versus rate, total interest paid, and payoff time under both.
scenes: Debt Loaded
Four debts load with balances and APRs.
Four debt cards with balance and APR, a total balance of $28,400.
Cards stack in at 80ms intervals; the total counts up and locks with a mono summary line.
Snowball Starts
The snowball pays the smallest balance first regardless of rate.
Left payoff track, debt cards ordered by balance ascending, cross-out stamps.
Cards cross out sequentially at 500ms intervals; each cross-out shrinks the balance to zero.
Avalanche Starts
The avalanche targets the highest APR first.
Right payoff track, debt cards ordered by APR descending, an interest-saved counter.
Parallel progress with the snowball, but the interest counter runs lower; both tracks share the same time axis.
Finish Line
Both reach zero; the avalanche saves $1,340 and 3 months.
Two race lanes converging to zero, a comparison card with months and interest.
Lane markers land at different months on the same axis; the comparison card reveals both figures side by side and holds.
vectors: Four 220x80 cards with balance, APR and a status stamp area
Two horizontal lanes with month ticks and a zero line
Rotated -8deg uppercase outline stamp with a 1.5px stroke
Circular markers that traverse their lane based on remaining balance
Three-row table: months, total interest, interest saved
physics: Both lanes share one time axis; different time scales would invalidate the comparison entirely.
Snowball visually clears cards faster at the start, which is the honest psychological benefit.
The avalanche's interest saving is the counterweight and must appear in the same frame as the finish.
Number of months and interest must come from the simulated amortization, not estimates.
data: const DEBT = { totalBalance: 28_400, debts: [{ name: 'Store Card', balance: 1_200, apr: 0.2699 }, { name: 'Credit Card', balance: 6_400, apr: 0.2249 }, { name: 'Auto Loan', balance: 8_800, apr: 0.0695 }, { name: 'Student Loan', balance: 12_000, apr: 0.051 }, snowballMonths: 34, avalancheMonths: 31, snowballInterest: 4_890, avalancheInterest: 3_550 };
notes: Simulate the amortization properly, at least monthly, including minimum payments. Both lanes must reconcile to the same total paid.

name: Chargeback Dispute Flow
hook: Evidence in, arbitration out, funds restored, on one timeline.
objective: Show the dispute lifecycle: chargeback filing, merchant evidence submission, network arbitration, and outcome notification.
scenes: Chargeback Filed
A cardholder files a dispute for $1,240 with reason code 'not as described'.
Dispute card with reason code, amount, and a filed timestamp, a case ID.
The reason code types in mono; the case ID stamps with a 200ms spring; the filed chip turns amber.
Merchant Evidence
The merchant uploads tracking, delivery proof and correspondence.
Three evidence upload tiles with file glyphs, progress rings, and a submission deadline chip.
Upload rings fill at 120ms intervals; the deadline chip counts down from 7 days in mono.
Arbitration Review
The network reviews both sides and issues a decision.
Balanced scale graphic with evidence weights on each side, a review status ladder of three stages.
Scale tilts toward the cardholder with a 400ms settle; the ladder steps light at 400ms intervals.
Funds Restored
The decision lands, funds return to the cardholder and the case closes.
Outcome card, restored funds arrow to the cardholder, closed status with a reason summary.
The funds arrow reverses the original charge path; the closed stamp lands with a 1.08 overshoot; hold.
vectors: 360x200 with reason code, amount, and a status rail
Three 140x100 tiles with a paper glyph and a progress ring
Amber pill with a mono countdown and a clock glyph
Central fulcrum with two weighted pans and a settling beam
Card with a decision label, amount restored and a closing rule

The scale tilts only once, slowly, and settles without oscillation.

name: Embedded Insurance
hook: A checkout toggle that mints a policy in under a second.
objective: Show embedded insurance at checkout: coverage offer, premium calculation, instant policy issuance and claims path.
scenes: Checkout
A $1,899 laptop sits in the cart with an assurance row beneath.
Checkout card, line items, an assurance row with a shield glyph and a 2.4% premium.
The assurance row highlights with a 2px indigo outline; the premium chip counts from 0.0% to 2.4%.
Toggle On
The micro-shield toggle flips and coverage terms expand.
Toggle at 56x32, an expanding details panel with 3 coverage bullets and an exclusion note.
The panel expands from 0 to its height over 320ms; bullets fade in at 80ms intervals; the exclusion line uses a smaller, muted style.
Policy Issued
A policy number is minted with an effective timestamp and a premium of $45.58.
Policy card with number, term, premium, and an instant-issue badge.
The policy number types at 24ms per character; the instant badge stamps in with a 180ms spring; the total updates once.
Claim Path
A claim button appears with a one-tap promise and a 48-hour target.
Claim CTA with a subtle pulse, a 48h SLA chip, and a coverage summary line.
The CTA pulses twice at 1.04 scale; the SLA chip fades in; everything settles to a still final frame.
vectors: Shield path 40px tall with a check glyph and a 1.5px stroke
Rounded track with a 24px knob and a subtle inner shadow
340x200 with policy number, term dates, premium and issuer line
Emerald pill with a clock glyph and a mono duration
Three-bullet block with consistent line heights
physics: Premium must be computed from the cart total and the displayed rate; the arithmetic is checked by viewers.
The exclusions line is not optional; an insurance demo without exclusions is a compliance problem.

name: Carbon Offset Checkout
hook: A checkout that measures grams of CO2 and grows a tree on the receipt.
objective: Show carbon-aware checkout: footprint estimation, offset pricing, contribution capture and verification record.
scenes: Order Summary
A $96 order is itemized and a footprint line appears.
Order card with three items, a footprint row in mono grams of CO2.
The footprint figure counts from 0 to 14.2 kg; the row gains a leaf glyph that fades in at completion.
Footprint Estimate
Shipping, packaging and product emissions break down.
A three-segment horizontal bar labeled SHIPPING, PACKAGING, PRODUCT with a total.
Segments grow left to right at 120ms offsets; a total rule draws beneath and the grams count in.
Offset Toggle

name: AI Financial Copilot
hook: A sentence typed in plain language turning into a live cash-flow forecast.
objective: Show an AI copilot workflow: natural-language intent, tool calls against real financial data, a generated forecast chart, and cited assumptions.
scenes: Prompt
The user types: 'What does cash runway look like if hiring slows by 30%?'
Prompt bar with a caret, a submit chip, and a small model badge.
Characters type at 26ms; the caret blinks at 530ms intervals; the submit chip lights when the last character lands.
Tool Calls
Three tool calls fire against ledger, payroll and forecast data.

Forecast Chart
The chart draws two paths: current plan and slowed hiring.
Dual-line forecast chart with a shaded runway area, month axis, and an intersection marker at the runway end.

Cited Answer

Answer card with a headline figure, three assumption rows with source tags, and a confidence note.
